title: Magnetic Properties of High-Entropy Alloy FeCoNiTi

recollection.starting_material: Equiatomic high-entropy alloy composed of Fe, Co, Ni, and Ti elements (powder or elemental buttons).
recollection.intervention: Arc-melting (or induction melting) to form an ingot followed by homogenization/annealing and possibly cold-rolling and further heat treatment; magnetic measurements carried out with VSM or SQUID.
recollection.structure: Predominantly single-phase FCC (with some BCC or ordered precipitates after annealing) solid solution; nanoscale lattice distortion from Ti addition.
recollection.mechanism: Ferromagnetic exchange among Fe, Co, and Ni atoms is moderated by lattice strain and potential ordering induced by Ti; annealing may promote short-range order or precipitates that pin domain walls, affecting coercivity.
recollection.results: Reported saturation magnetization on the order of 1.0–1.3 T, coercivity ~50–150 Oe, and Curie temperature near 900–1000 K; annealing slightly increases Ms and lowers Hc, indicating improved chemical homogeneity and reduced lattice strain (all values approximate).

score.note: The recollection partially identifies arc melting but incorrectly adds homogenization, annealing, and rolling while missing rapid quenching and the C14-dominant comparison alloy. Its single-phase FCC description contradicts the observed fcc+C14 dual-phase structure. The mechanism is only generic, missing Ti-sublattice antiferromagnetic coupling, phase-specific transitions, orbital effects, and C14-assisted domain-wall pinning. The reported coercivity is far below the actual 667 Oe, and it misses the 1084, 214, and 168 K transitions.
